answer: A stake-weighted reputation graph makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent identity must lock a deposit that grows along a vine of verified interactions, so a newcomer cannot instantly match an established peer. A comet of cheap, freshly minted identities burns through its deposit the moment it misbehaves, while a relic of long, honest service accumulates weight that cannot be bought overnight. Forging a thousand fake agents therefore costs a thousand deposits and years of history, far more than any single fraud can recover.
